caption: The drawing depicts a detailed line illustration of a banjo-style wall clock, shown in both front and side views on a vertically oriented sheet. The clock is topped with a sculpted eagle with outspread wings, perched on a rectangular pedestal. The round clock face, labeled "L. Curtis Patent," displays Roman numerals and two clock hands indicating the time. Below the clock face, the body tapers downward and features decorative panels, one with floral motifs and another with what appears to be a shield or emblem. At the lower end of the body is a larger, circular panel featuring a nautical scene with ships and water, as well as a human figure in the foreground. Ornate scrollwork extends below this panel, creating a decorative finial. Dotted lines accentuate the framing of the clock sections. The side view to the right presents the clock's depth and shows the three-dimensional aspects of the eagle, panels, and scrollwork. The illustration is monochrome, drawn in black ink on a yellowed, off-white background. Measurement markings on the right indicate the clock's height as 47 inches and note the scale as 3/16. Handwritten text at the bottom identifies the object as a "Banjo Clock #30.120.54 Room M.T. Met. Mus."
title: Clock
